topIssues.label: Food arrives cold or at the wrong temperature
topIssues.whatToDo: Make sure hot food stays hot at the pickup counter. Use heat lamps or insulated boxes. Quickly check the food temperature before handing it to the customer.
topIssues.rationale: Shows up almost every month since February 2024. Affects pickup and delivery the most, and is one of the fastest ways to upset a customer.
topIssues.exampleQuote: While at the restaurant, I had to wait for an hour to receive my order, which is unacceptable. To make matters worse, when it finally about to eat, it wasn't cooked as requested (well done), as evidenced by the photos. What a disappointment! I won't be returning and cannot recomm

topIssues.label: Portions are too small for the price
topIssues.whatToDo: Weigh and measure each dish daily. Put a portion guide at every cooking station. Retrain cooks on correct serving sizes.
topIssues.rationale: Comes up every month from March 2024 onward. Customers feel cheated even when the food is good.
topIssues.exampleQuote: Ordered from Limesalt. Food was very bland and small portioned for the price. Tortilla chips tasted like they were from from a store bought bag. This was my fear when ordering from wonder, that since they have a broad menu with so many "restaurants". The quality is definitely imp

topIssues.label: Long wait times to get food
topIssues.whatToDo: Count how many orders are in the kitchen at peak times. Add a second cook or another order screen if needed. Tell customers an honest wait time when they order.
topIssues.rationale: Appears in nearly every month. Gets worse at lunch and dinner. Drives away repeat visits even when the food itself is fine.
topIssues.exampleQuote:
Very bad this store worker and very slow
😡

topIssues.label: Food quality changes from shop to shop and visit to visit
topIssues.whatToDo: Put one lead cook in charge of each restaurant inside the shop. Have them taste every dish before it leaves. Make a photo guide of how each dish should look.
topIssues.rationale: Shows up every month. Customers notice when the same dish tastes different at different shops or on different days, and they start to trust the brand less.
topIssues.exampleQuote: Tried probably 4 of their “different chefs” not a single thing was good

topIssues.label: Orders are missing items or have the wrong ingredients
topIssues.whatToDo: Double-check every bag before it leaves the counter against the receipt. Put one person in charge of the pickup station during the rush. Use a checklist for orders that include food from more than one restaurant.
topIssues.rationale: Shows up every month, in dine-in, pickup, and delivery. Forces refunds and makes customers stop trusting the ordering system.
topIssues.exampleQuote: I’ve tried a few of the cuisines here at Wonder. Very average, nothing too exciting. On this day I wondered the zesty chicken souvlaki bowl. The rice was all clumped together, the chicken was dry, and the order was missing the pita chips and green goddess dressing.

topWins.label: Food is consistently good and fresh
topWins.whatToDo: Check kitchen prep, storage, and cooking temperatures every week across all 14 shops. Train cooks to plate the same way and to check that ingredients are fresh. Taste finished dishes before they leave the kitchen.
topWins.rationale: Shows up every single month from January 2024 through May 2026. Customers reward this more than anything else.
topWins.exampleQuote: The best food in Brooklyn ! I love it !

topWins.label: Fast service and quick orders
topWins.whatToDo: Track how long an order takes from the order screen to the customer's hand, every day, in each shop. Aim for 8 minutes for dine-in and 6 minutes for pickup. Add staff at lunch and dinner peaks. If the order-screen line is more than 5 minutes long, open another register.
topWins.rationale: Customers praise speed every single month, almost as often as they praise the food itself.
topWins.exampleQuote: Very good food and fast service! The  wings are amazing

topWins.label: Friendly, attentive, and helpful staff
topWins.whatToDo: Hire for attitude. Train everyone to greet each customer within 30 seconds. Once a month, recognize staff who get named in reviews. Coach managers to set the tone and to spot anyone who seems rushed or dismissive.
topWins.rationale: Comes up every month. Friendly staff is one of the top things customers mention alongside food and speed.
topWins.exampleQuote: The food was well cooked and customers service was phenomenal

topWins.label: Easy to order from several restaurants in one visit
topWins.whatToDo: Try a multi-restaurant order every day to spot-check. Make sure the kitchen times everything so all the food arrives hot together. Train staff to suggest good combos for families. Fix the app so it shows which restaurant's food is ready first.
topWins.rationale: Mentioned in 20+ months. Customers love the format, but small mistakes — cold items, timing mismatches — cost repeat visits.
topWins.exampleQuote: All the best chefs in one place this is a can't lose food was great its definitely a place I order from frequently

topWins.label: Clean and well-kept shops
topWins.whatToDo: Use an hourly cleaning checklist for the dining area and the kitchen. Pick one staff member each shift to walk the shop every 30 minutes. Take photos of bathrooms and dining areas at open, lunch, dinner, and close, and post them in the staff area.
topWins.rationale: Comes up in 15+ months. Customers expect clean shops as the minimum — when it's missing, they leave bad reviews and stop coming back.
topWins.exampleQuote: The place is clean and so far  the food has been amazing. Great customer service as well.
